subject: Acme: request for penetration assessment deliverables and verification timeline
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: RedwoodSec <report@redwoodsec.io>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -0400
Subject: Request: deliverables from penetration assessment + remediation evidence

Hi Sean,

Thanks for sharing the penetration assessment with our security team. We finished an internal read-through and have a few follow-ups before we can sign off on our vendor security review. Specifically we need:

- The full pen test report PDF (including supplemental test vectors) and any PoC artifacts from RedwoodSec.
- Concrete evidence that the three critical findings affecting our integration are closed:
  * privilege escalation (SUID-like escalation in auth service)
  * missing authentication/authorization logging for token lifecycle events
  * sensitive config values in an unaudited keystore backup (secrets exposure)

For each finding please provide: short remediation summary, test steps you ran to validate the fix, timestamps (UTC) of when fixes were deployed to staging and production, and logs/screenshots/traces showing the failing behavior is no longer reproducible.

Our timeline: we need artifacts by EOD 2026-08-20 to keep to our procurement schedule. If that timeline is not possible, send an interim ETA and any compensating controls you have in place.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if it helps clarify what we need.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Security Lead, Acme Logistics

Attachments: acme-questions-0809.pdf (list of specific test cases)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, RedwoodSec <report@redwoodsec.io>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: deliverables from penetration assessment + remediation evidence

Lena — thanks for the note and the clear list. We take these findings seriously. Ill coordinate delivery of the report and the evidence package.

Action items Im assigning now:
- Karthik, please prepare a one-page remediation summary per finding and bundle the verification artifacts (logs, screenshots, test scripts). Call out UTC timestamps and the environment (staging/prod).
- Irene, please collect SOC2-relevant artifacts and retention policy notes that map back to these items.
- Marissa, will you confirm with RedwoodSec whether theyll re-run the three failing test cases against our patched staging environment and include the PoC files they used?

Lena — well aim to have an initial evidence bundle to you by 2026-08-19 EOD and the final package (including RedwoodSec verification) by 2026-08-20 per your procurement window. If anything slips Ill raise it immediately.

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: deliverables from penetration assessment + remediation evidence

On Wed, Aug 12, 2026 at 12:03 PM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Lena — thanks for the note and the clear list. I'll coordinate delivery of the report and the evidence package.

Folks — a quick engineering update on the three items Lena called out and the verification plan: 

1) Privilege escalation (auth service):
- Root cause: overly permissive role mapping for internal service-to-service calls; test harness showed a path that allowed elevated privileges when client context contained legacy roleClaim.
- Fix: tightened role mapper logic, added defensive checks in the auth middleware, and added an explicit deny-list for legacy roleClaim values.
- Deployment plan: patch pushed to staging 2026-08-17 03:10:00 UTC; smoke tests run 2026-08-17 03:45:00 UTC.
- Verification: unit + integration tests updated; RedwoodSec to execute targeted exploit attempt on staging (ticket SEC-4521). PoF artifacts: exploit script, request/response captures, and mitigation logs.

2) Auth/authorization logging gaps:
- Root cause: token rotation events were logged at DEBUG only in older runtime; switched to INFO for lifecycle events and forwarded to central audit pipeline.
- Fix: logging level changes, additional structured fields (token_id, user_hash, request_id).
- Deployment plan: staged rollout began 2026-08-17 04:30:00 UTC; full rollout to prod scheduled 2026-08-18 02:00:00 UTC (can be accelerated if Acme needs earlier).
- Verification: sample logs with redacted identifiers included in the evidence bundle.

3) Keystore backup containing sensitive config:
- Root cause: backup tooling included an extra path; backup job now excludes /secrets/ and we rotated impacted keys.
- Fix: keystore rotation executed; new backup policy and automated preflight check added to CI.
- Deployment plan: rotation completed 2026-08-16 22:10:00 UTC; new backups verified 2026-08-17 01:05:00 UTC.
- Verification: keystore rotation command output (keystore-rotation-commands.txt) and rotation audit log excerpt.

ETA and evidence cadence:
- Initial evidence bundle (staging test outputs, patch diff, sample logs): 2026-08-19 EOD (UTC).
- Full package with RedwoodSec verification report and PoC removal confirmation: 2026-08-20 EOD (UTC).

Attachments included in this email: kv-cache-remediation.patch, keystore-rotation-commands.txt.

If Acme wants to accelerate prod rollout for the logging fix, we can shift the prod deploy earlier by 12–24 hours; flag me and Ill prioritize.

Thanks,
Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Infra

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: deliverables from penetration assessment + remediation evidence

Hi Lena / Sean —

Thanks for looping me in. A couple compliance-specific notes to make the handoff smoother: 

- Evidence naming convention: were using RDW-EVID-<account>-<finding>-<YYYYMMDD>-<artifact> so Acme can map items back to the SOC2 control matrix.
- Retention and scope: logs and audit trails well include are retained for 90 days by default; if Acme requires longer retention for this review we can prepare an extended export (may take +1 business day).
- What well provide in the package: remediation summary, patch diff, deploy timestamps (UTC), sample logs (redacted UIDs), keystore rotation audit, and an index file that maps artifacts to the SIG/SOC2 control IDs.

Drive folder (read-only link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleEvidenceLink
Document index: RDW-EVID-ACME-INDEX-20260819.csv

Quick question for Acme: do you need raw request/response captures for the privilege escalation test, or are the sanitized captures (request IDs + response codes + timestamps) sufficient for your risk team? If you prefer raw captures we can coordinate an NDA-addendum and will deliver via secure transfer.

Irene Choi
Director, Compliance & Security Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Lena — delivering the evidence bundle per the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

Whats included (archive + links):
- evidence-archive-acme-20260819.zip (attached) — contains:
  * RDW-EVID-ACME-PRIVESC-20260819/
    - exploit-script.txt
    - exploit-requests.har (sanitized)
    - mitigation-logs.txt (timestamps: 2026-08-17T03:45:00Z -> 2026-08-19T02:00:00Z)
  * RDW-EVID-ACME-AUTHLOG-20260819/
    - sample-logs-redacted.log
    - logging-config-diff.patch
  * RDW-EVID-ACME-KEYSTORE-20260819/
    - keystore-rotation-commands.txt
    - rotation-audit-excerpt.txt
  * RDW-EVID-ACME-INDEX-20260819.csv (mapping of artifacts to controls)
- Drive folder (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleEvidenceLink
- RedwoodSec verification: supplemental report at https://redwoodsec.io/reports/rdw-acme-2026 (they confirmed staging exploitation attempts failed post-patch).

Summary: fixes were deployed to staging on 2026-08-17 UTC and rolled into prod for the logging changes on 2026-08-18 UTC. Keystore rotation occurred 2026-08-16 UTC and the audit excerpt in the archive shows key IDs rotated and previous backups invalidated. RedwoodSec re-ran the three test cases against staging and included their verification notes in the supplemental report.

Next steps: please confirm whether the sanitized captures are adequate or if Acme requires raw captures. Also confirm receipt of the evidence ZIP so I can mark the procurement ticket as "evidence provided."

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if youd like a guided walkthrough of the bundle.

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
